narrative.origin_story: Jordan Chen runs operations for a holding that built five ventures in three years.
narrative.manifesto:
Every expansion produces entropy. Not because anyone fails. Because growth, without a field that holds it together, *is* entropy.

The first year, three ventures know each other by name. The third year, twelve ventures, three time zones, four regulatory regimes, eight currencies, and forty endeavors all run in parallel. Coordination, which used to be a Slack channel, is now a problem.

Most ecosystems solve this by centralizing. They appoint a control plane that owns every decision, every record, every customer relationship. The brands lose their soul. The system gets predictable, expensive, and slow.

Cosmos chooses the other path. We are gravity, not government. We declare the canonical objects every brand reads. We propagate state changes between brands at sub-second latency. We publish governance — not as policy, but as version-controlled doctrine that any brand can fork or amend.

We did not invent this way of working. The [GitLab handbook](https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/) proved that operations-by-publication scales. The [Palantir Ontology](https://blog.palantir.com/the-foundry-ontology-9c87fc7f78b3) proved that a shared object model lets independent teams compose. [Atlassian's System of Work](https://www.atlassian.com/teamwork) proved that interoperability is a category. We are the synthesis: gravity by ontology, governance by doctrine, autonomy by default.

You will not see Cosmos most days. You will feel it.

---

steps: Treat PAD as the portable content and behavior payload
